newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN board meet Thurs may reveal troubles.
newsitem.headline: GAN board meet Thurs may reveal troubles.

text.p: Another tale of of woe in France's financial sector, and the cost of sorting it out, should be made clearer on Thursday after a board meeting at troubled, state-owned insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN).

Like beleaguered state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais, GAN is negotiating a rescue plan with the government to stem huge losses from the property business and other woes which have been plaguing it for several years.
A spokeswoman for the company said the board would meet on Thursday afternoon and that a statement could be issued after the meeting, but she declined to elaborate.
The finance ministry has also remained tightlipped on its talks with GAN, which it wants to privatise.

While the scale of likely the rescue pales beside repeated bailouts for Credit Lyonnais since the bank's runaway expansion brought it to the brink of bankruptcy, the government will, as in the case of Credit Lyonnais, have to get approval for the cash injection from the European Commission in Brussels.

European Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on January 22 he was expecting a request from Paris for clearance to give more aid to GAN, after a 2.9-billion-franc injection which he already approved in July 1995.
Analysts say the likelihood is a government rescue package costing anything between 10 and 20 billion francs.

The less costly scenario would involve further provisioning of some seven billion francs at the UIC property arm and the Baticredit property defeasance structure and close to three billion francs in technical provisions in insurance.
Further more conservative provisioning in non-life and life insurance and and more dramatic plans for shutting down UIC businesses compeletely could push the bill up, they say.

The company is not expected to produce its 1996 accounts until April and the meeting on Thursday is more likely to focus on the provisioning needs following a special audit report recently presented to the group.
